entries.title: Judges 15:1
segments:
The time of wheat-harvest; in May. 
 
  A kid; as a present, and in token of reconciliation. 
 
Those who have been wronged or offended should ever be ready to forgive, and take all suitable measures for reconciliation with those who have wronged or offended them.

entries.title: Judges 15:2
segments: The friendship of the wicked is sometimes more hazardous than their enmity, and the course they propose to remove one difficulty often plunges those who follow it into a greater.

entries.title: Judges 15:3
segments: If there must be a contest, we should be careful not ourselves to be the sinful cause of it.

entries.title: Judges 15:4
segments: Foxes; the original word includes also jackals, which are abundant in Palestine, and easily caught.

entries.title: Judges 15:6
segments: By doing wrong to avoid an evil, we take a course which will bring upon us either that or something worse.

entries.title: Judges 15:8
segments:
Top; fissure, cleft, or cavern. 
 
  Etam; supposed to be south of Timnath, in the tribe of Judah.

entries.title: Judges 15:9
segments: Lehi; the place where Samson with a jawbone smote the Philistines, and on that account called Lehi, which means, in Hebrew, jawbone.

entries.title: Judges 15:11
segments: The professed friends of God may be so besotted and debased by sin as to join with his enemies, and oppose those who would save them and their children from degradation and ruin.

entries.title: Judges 15:14
segments: The triumph of the wicked is short, and when they are most confident of success they are often nearest to destruction.

entries.title: Judges 15:16
segments: The weakest and most contemptible instruments may become mighty through God to the destruction of the most powerful of his foes.

entries.title: Judges 15:18
segments: Great successes are often, in the course of providence, followed by great trials, that all who have been favored may feel their dependence on God and their constant need of his help.

entries.title: Judges 15:19
segments: In the jaw; or, in Lehi.  Compare

.  That this latter is the right rendering appears from the fact that a permanent fountain was produced by this interposition of God, which continued to flow in the writer's day. 
 
  En-hakkore; fountain of him that called, that is, upon God in prayer. 
 
When men are sensible of their insufficiency, and look up with a humble, believing, and affectionate heart to God, he is able and willing to help them and cause them to raise a permanent memorial to his praise.
